claims.location: web page, Results ('Thermal tolerance') and Discussion
claims.quote: compared to our values of 31.2°C and 40.7°C
claims.conditions: laboratory CTmax (loss of equilibrium) at a ramp of ~0.3 °C/min (measured 0.26 ± 0.04); pumpkinseed from Lake Cromwell (Station de Biologie des Laurentides, Québec), small fish (mean TL 7.3–8.1 cm per group, 6.9–9.6 g); acclimated to 10, 15, 20 (fall groups) and 20, 25, 30 °C (summer group); results range 31.20 ± 0.46 to 40.66 ± 0.23 °C; CTmax rose ~0.47 °C per degree of acclimation; the fish carried a natural gradient of parasite infection
claims.note: The values are the 10 °C and 30 °C groups' means, as the paper says. The authors note the fast ramp: Rooke et al. 2017 found ~30 and 39.5 °C at 10 and 30 °C with a slower ramp (0.066 °C/min), and fish in the wild warming at natural rates may tolerate less. 30 °C is a heat-wave-plus-2 °C scenario, not a lake condition.
